objective: Register a separate, finite future implementation of provider-neutral APBRA authentication/session and Microsoft Entra External ID as the first qualified live OIDC profile; this governance PR changes no application behavior.
requirements: Jira APBRA-172 under APBRA-160; Haseeb owner APBRA-172 package 2026-10-02 and PLAN comment 10385.

Authenticate only through a deployment-qualified trusted provider profile. Validate authorization code with PKCE, state, nonce, exact issuer/audience/signature/lifetime/subject and trusted discovery/JWKS; prevent mix-up, replay, open redirect and arbitrary browser-supplied trust.

Bind validated provider-qualified issuer/subject to durable APBRA identity without email/domain/UPN/IdP-group authority or silent cross-provider account linking. Preserve exact invitation semantics and fail-closed company membership and private-case access.

Issue APBRA-owned revocable server sessions with secure browser cookies, CSRF protection, expiry and current identity/membership/resource rechecks; avoid provider token retention and do not request Graph, Power BI/Fabric or Azure management scopes for basic login.

Provide provider-neutral sign-in/session/logout UI; deterministic local/test identity stays local/test-only, hosted mode requires a qualified live provider; no unauthorised first-user company creation in this task.
adrs: Microsoft Entra External ID is first qualified OIDC adapter, not core identity architecture or a deployment requirement; later providers require separate qualification.

Provider trust is deployment/bootstrap configuration, not self-qualified Tenant Settings or browser input. Secrets use protected deployment references and never enter source, normal rows, browser, logs or task contracts.
External authentication, APBRA company membership, exact private-resource grant, entitlement, Power BI/Fabric consent and Azure management authority are distinct.

APBRA-151 owns server-transactional company creation and initial COMPANY_OWNER; APBRA-172 may expose an authenticated no-membership onboarding state only. APBRA-173 owns hosted Azure preview provisioning.
Preserve APBRA-175 portability and NO HARDCODING. No customer-varying tenant, issuer, provider endpoint, cloud, region or commercial value is compiled into core logic.

acceptance_criteria: Later implementation branch changes only the 24 exact literal allowed paths; this registration branch changes only seven governance files and no application/runtime path.
Entra External ID is a qualified live adapter behind provider-neutral profile/binding/session contracts; deterministic simulator remains local/test-only and hosted fail-closed.
Cross-provider same-email, mutable profile claims, external tenant/domain/group, invitation mismatch, stale membership and wrong resource cannot grant APBRA role or access.
Exact issuer/audience/signature/key/lifetime/state/nonce/PKCE and redirect protections, session lifecycle and safe logout have deterministic negative tests and PostgreSQL/browser coverage.
APBRA-151 company creation and APBRA-173 cloud provisioning remain separate; no automatic company owner, Graph/Power BI/Fabric/ARM consent, other-provider implementation or billing.
Live Entra qualification is separately evidenced with explicit owner setup and cost/security approval; deterministic tests alone never claim live provider or production readiness.
verification_required: Focused APBRA-172 exact source/task hash, path and negative mutation tests plus historical source-order tests.
Full bootstrap suite, standalone scripts/check_bootstrap.py and scripts/check_ci_policy.py; exact changed-path audit, git diff --check, history-aware secret scan where locally supported.
Later implementation: complete API pytest, Ruff, strict mypy, PostgreSQL 17 migration upgrade/downgrade and integration, web unit/type/build/Playwright and hosted CI.
Hosted APBRA Bootstrap CI on exact registration PR head, genuinely separate exact-head review, then Haseeb-only manual registration merge before a new implementation branch.
Later product PR requires hosted CI, separately evidenced real Entra qualification where applicable, independent review and Haseeb-only manual merge.
out_of_scope: Any application/runtime change in this governance PR; any later path outside the 24 literal allowlist.
APBRA-151 company creation, initial owner transaction or broad multi-company UX redesign; APBRA-173 IaC, DNS, cloud resources, production deployment and spend.
Google/Apple/enterprise SAML implementation, SCIM/JIT, domain auto-join, cross-provider account linking, automatic IdP-group roles, entitlement/billing/pricing.
Microsoft Graph directory discovery, Power BI/Fabric publishing/consent, Azure Resource Manager permissions, paid or live provider calls without separate approval.
Dependency/lockfile/workflow changes, weakened checks, historical task/source rewrite, self-approval, direct main write, auto-merge or agent merge.
escalate_when: Any required implementation path, dependency, workflow or governance file lies outside this exact registration and future allowlist.
Accepted sources conflict, a provider/client credential or cost/security decision is required, or APBRA-151 ownership boundaries cannot be preserved.
Mandatory validation, hosted CI, independent exact-head review or Haseeb manual merge gate is absent, skipped, failed or stale.
